title: Atom: Low-bit Quantization for Efficient and Accurate LLM Serving
technique: 4-bit weight-activation quantization with mixed-precision outlier channels, fine-grained group quantization, dynamic activation quant, 4-bit KV cache, fused kernels (FlashInfer, PagedAttention)

optimized_metrics.evidence: To maximize LLMs' serving throughput, we introduce Atom, a low-bit quantization method that achieves high throughput improvements with negligible accuracy loss.
while maintaining the same latency target
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: Average decode latency per token. (Fig 11b caption)

optimized_metrics.evidence: low-bit quantization method that achieves high throughput improvements with negligible accuracy loss

headline_claim.text: Atom improves end-to-end throughput (token/s) by up to 7.73x compared to the FP16 and by 2.53x compared to INT8 quantization, while maintaining the same latency target.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 10(b) average decode latency per token
Fig 10(c) throughput at fixed GPU memory

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We show the end-to-end throughput, i.e., generated tokens per second, in Figure 10(a).
metric_definitions.notes: Output (generated) tokens/s, single GPU; batch size varied 8-256; dashed lines are simulated where memory exceeds GPU.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We measure the latency as the average decoding time of each token, without considering the queuing time.
metric_definitions.notes: Called 'end-to-end latency' but is average per-token decode time, queueing excluded. Latency target = 'Tolerable Latency' line of 100 ms in Fig 10.

slo_spec: Fixed latency target of 100 ms per decoded token (human reading speed); throughput compared at that latency with larger batch enabled by memory savings
load_regime: fixed batch size sweep (8-256), ShareGPT prefill/decode length distribution, multi-round chats as separate requests, FCFS
tradeoff_acknowledged: Fine-grained group quantization contributes the major kernel overhead (~8% for mixed precision fusion); accuracy cost small (e.g. 0.3 WikiText2 perplexity increase for Llama-65B)
hardware: RTX 4090 (24GB) with simulation beyond memory; A100 kernels
workloads: ShareGPT; WikiText2, PTB, C4; zero-shot tasks
extractor_notes: Throughput is the objective under a fixed per-token latency target (100 ms); 'end-to-end latency' excludes queueing. Rare case of a quantization paper stating a throughput-at-latency objective.
load_class_quote: We vary the batch size from 8 to 256 ... All requests are served in a First-Come-First-Served manner. When a request is finished, we re-fill the on-the-fly batch with a new request following continous batching (§5.3; no arrival process)
